title: How Oft Have Sin and Satan Strove
description: How Oft Have Sin and Satan Strove in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 139, headed “Hope in the covenant; or, God's promise and truth unchangeable, Heb. 6. 17 18 19”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How oft have sin and Sa-tan strove To rend my soul from thee, my God, But ev-er-last-ing is thy love, And Je-sus seals it with his blood.

lines: How oft have sin and Satan strove
To rend my soul from thee, my God,
And Jesus seals it with his blood.
The oath and promise of the Lord
Join to confirm the wondrous grace;
And fills all heaven with endless praise.
My soul to this dear refuge flies:
Hope is my anchor firm and strong,
While tempests blow, and billows rise.
The gospel bears my spirits up;
Lays the foundation for my hope
In oaths, and promises, and blood.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
